walkthrough:
In the right-angled triangle $\triangle XYC$ (with right angle at $X$), use basic trigonometry:
$$\sin(\angle XYC) = \frac{\text{opposite}}{\text{hypotenuse}} = \frac{CX}{YC} = \frac{9}{11}$$
$$\angle XYC = \sin^{-1}\left(\frac{9}{11}\right) \approx 0.95818 \approx 0.9582\text{ radians} \quad (\text{to 4 s.f.})$$

ai_rubric.Circular Measure: Uses $\sin(\angle XYC) = 9/11$ (B1) to show $\angle XYC = 0.9582\text{ rad}$.

walkthrough:
Calculate the length of segment $XY$ using the Pythagorean theorem:
$$XY = \sqrt{YC^2 - CX^2} = \sqrt{11^2 - 9^2} = \sqrt{121 - 81} = \sqrt{40} = 2\sqrt{10} \approx 6.3246\text{ cm}$$

Calculate the length of the straight base $AB$:
$$AB = AY + BX - XY = 11 + 9 - \sqrt{40} = 20 - 6.3246 = 13.6754\text{ cm}$$

Calculate the lengths of the two circular arcs $AC$ and $BC$:
$$\text{Arc } AC = r_Y \theta_Y = 11 \times 0.95818 \approx 10.5400\text{ cm}$$
$$\text{Arc } BC = r_X \theta_X = 9 \times \frac{\pi}{2} = 4.5\pi \approx 14.1372\text{ cm}$$

Sum all boundary pieces to determine the total perimeter of region $ABC$:
$$\text{Perimeter} = AB + \text{Arc } AC + \text{Arc } BC = 13.6754 + 10.5400 + 14.1372 = 38.3526 \approx 38.4\text{ cm} \quad (\text{to 3 s.f.})$$

ai_rubric.Perimeter of Circular Shapes: Calculates $XY = \sqrt{40}$ (M1, A1). Finds $AB = 20 - \sqrt{40}$ (B1 FT). Calculates arc $AC$ (M1) and arc $BC$ (M1). Obtains total perimeter $38.4\text{ cm}$ (A1).
